name: Sapphire FUE

lead: Sapphire FUE is a hair transplant in which the recipient channels are cut with sapphire blades rather than steel. Clinics describe finer incisions, about 0.5 to 1.0 mm, that may allow denser placement, less bleeding, faster healing and less visible scarring for a denser hairline.

Follicles are extracted as in standard FUE, then implanted into the channels. Evidence comparing blade types is limited: a 2026 paper compared sapphire and steel blades, and a registered trial studied a topical agent for wound healing after sapphire FUE.

paras: It follows the standard FUE routine under local anaesthetic, with sapphire-tipped blades used to make the recipient sites before grafts are placed. Hair grows in over the following months.
Risks are those of FUE in general, such as swelling, shock loss and folliculitis.

angle.text: Sapphire FUE is promoted as giving hair transplants finer incisions, denser graft placement and faster healing, for a fuller hairline with less visible scarring. The restored hair is visible once it grows in, while comparisons of blade types are limited.

lead: Sapphire FUE is a follicular unit extraction hair transplant in which recipient sites are made with sapphire blades instead of steel [1]. Grokipedia says the blades are sharper and finer, which may allow denser placement, less bleeding, faster healing and less visible scarring [1]; these are unverified descriptions from an AI-generated source.
A 2026 paper compared sapphire and steel FUE blades alongside forceps methods and treatment times [2], and a registered trial studied topical rifamycin SV for wound healing after sapphire FUE [3].

paras: A 2026 study in the Journal of Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery compared sapphire versus steel FUE blades, single versus double forceps implantation, half-head versus full-head surgeries and one- versus two-day procedures [2]. A completed registered trial of 70 participants studied topical rifamycin SV for wound healing after sapphire FUE [3].
